candidates.computation_change_reason: The multi-tier header maps pollutants to several parallel criteria families (instream waste concentration, domestic supply, irrigation, livestock/wildlife, acute/chronic aquatic, human health, TMDL need); different readings of which column family is enforceable for a given parameter change the applicable discharge limit.

Ambient and effluent concentration cells are blank while derived instream columns and some criteria columns read 0 or finite numbers; treating blanks as no-data versus implicit zero changes both which limit applies (e.g., 70 domestic vs 5300 human health vs 1E+100 placeholders) and whether missing-effluent evidence is documented zero or unresolved.

The same row mixes 1E+100 sentinel values with finite acute/chronic aquatic criteria (19, 15) and a domestic criterion of 1; interpreting 1E+100 as no numeric limit versus a literal cap, and choosing among domestic, aquatic, and human-health columns, changes which enforceable limit is used for exceedance comparison.

MQL is absent while other pollutants list quantitation limits; whether that omission means no detection requirement, inherited default, or incomplete table entry affects monitoring-obligation scope, whether measurements below an unknown MQL can be compared to limits, and how missing/no-result evidence for this parameter should be classified.

The section label partitions the pollutant list into groups that may correspond to different analyte classes or analytical methods; interpreting it as operative grouping versus mere table formatting can change which parameters are in scope for limit selection and associated monitoring requirements.

Every listed pollutant shows Need TMDL as N/A; reading N/A as confirming no TMDL-based limit applies versus as unspecified/unknown changes whether TMDL-driven limits or supplemental monitoring obligations are excluded from A/B computations.
